verdicts.reasoning:
I reproduced the finding with my own setup. I did not use the finder's scripts or their worktree. The injected-CNXML check at line 111 of the corpus test uses `includes`, so it cannot tell a replaced caption from one that keeps its English and adds the token. Under a mutant that removes the clear-out loop, both corpus tests pass. A strict check (`textContent.trim() === token`) gives the same counts as `includes` on the unmutated code, in every context and in both books, so switching costs nothing. Under the mutant, the strict check drops to 0 in every context that goes through applyFigureCaptionDom.

`top` stays at 510 (chemistry) and 457 (organic) under the mutant. That is expected: top-level captions are written by buildFigure, which has its own clear-out, so they never reach the mutated helper. This also explains why the finder's organic dump showed only example captions. In chemistry the mutant damages 115 captions (83 note, 31 example, 1 exercise).

One part of the finding is overstated. The line "readers would see English and Icelandic" suggests the full test suite would miss the regression. It does not. I ran the same 7 inject/caption test files on the unmutated and mutated copies and compared the failing tests by name. The mutant adds exactly one failure: `tools/__tests__/cnxml-inject.test.js` "buildNoteDom figure inside para (C13) > still translates the kept figure caption". That test came from commit 184a0da69 on 2026-07-27, before §C148, and its exact `<caption>…</caption>` match catches the English left in place. It catches this mutant only because the helper is shared and its fixture is a note. For captions kept inside example and exercise containers, the corpus test is the only pin, and it cannot see an append.

So this is not a merge blocker, since the C13 test covers the shared helper today. It is still a real gap in the test that owns this failure shape (English still present), and the fix is one token on line 111 at measured zero cost.

Scope limit: apply the strict check to line 111 only, not to the render check on line 113. On the unmutated code, strict equality in the rendered output matched 0 of 510 chemistry captions and 1 of 457 organic ones, because the rendered `<figcaption>` starts with a "Mynd N.M" figure label. "Mynd undefined.N" in my dumps comes from my probe not passing a chapter number; it is not a defect.
